## Diffusion

There are several steps to incorporating the diffusion data into the
`MD2DF` table.

1.  Run the *julia* `MD2` program to measure average particle mean
    displacements over time for each run. This will add executions to
    each run.
2.  Update the `MD2DF` table with the new execution data.
3.  Read in the raw diffusion data files.
4.  Create average diffusion data for each time delta (the raw data has
    several raw measurements at each time delta).
5.  Fit the diffusion data to a linear model for each run.
6.  Add the diffusion data to the `MD2DF` table.

Below are the counts of the data runs that have been heated or cooled.

```{r}
knitr::kable( MD2DF.N[ itype %in% c( "Cool", "Heat"), 
                       .(count = .N), by = itype])
```

### Diffusion Executions

Rather than being selective, we will make diffusion runs on all of the
heated/cooled runs. Following what we did in
[ReRun2024.pdf](ReRun2024.pdf), we will create a file list and a run
number list for import into *julia*.

```{r}
#| eval: false
drn <- MD2DF.N[ itype %in% c( "Heat", "Cool"), run]
cat( '["',
     paste( drn, collapse = '", "'), '"] \n', sep = "")
lfn <- strsplit( sapply( drn, \(fn) last( list.files( td, 
                                             paste(fn, "*.jld2", sep = ".")))),
                  "[.]")

as.integer(sapply( seq_along( lfn), \(i) lfn[[i]][3]))
```

### Updating `MD2DF.N`

Twenty 5,000-step executions of 139 files in 719 seconds is about 19.3
thousand-step runs per second, or 0.052s per thousand-step execution.
The system failed to process all the new diffusion runs in one call of
`MD2DFfile()`, possibly due to memory allocation errors. Since there are
only eight new series, we'll process them one-by-one.

```{r}
#| label: MD2DF.N2
MD2DF.N2 <- MD2DFfile( "../MD2DF.N2.RDS", td, "S3.0008h*.scalars.csv", 
                       df = MD2DF.N,
```

```{r}
MD2DF.P <- data.table::copy(MD2DF.O)
MD2DF.P$itype <- with( MD2DF.O, # Tag energy type
      ifelse( series %in% c("S1","S2"), "Init", # Asll S1 & S2 were simple inits
            ifelse( !grepl( "h", energy), "Init", # If no "H", then init.
                    ifelse( grepl( "0008|0009|0010|0011", energy), 
                            # these were heated
                            "Heat", "Cool") # else they were cooled.
                    )
            )
      )
# Tag the originating energy as the hseries
setkey( MD2DF.P, ke.mean.rs)
MD2DF.P[, hseries := fifelse( itype == "Init", "Init", 
                              substring( energy, 1, 4))]
saveRDS( MD2DF.P, "../MD2DF.P.RDS" )
```

### Reading in Diffusion Data

We can find all of the diffusion files via the following expressions and
function.

```{r}
#| label: read_diff
read_diff <- function( td, runname) { 
   # returns a data.table with diffusion data
   # td is the test data directory
   # runname is a filename ala list.files( td, glob2rx( "*.diff.txt"))
   filename <- list.files( td, runname, full.names = TRUE)
   #print( filename)
   dd <- data.table::fread( filename)
   nrdd <- nrow( dd)
   ddcols <- colnames( dd)
   timecols <- ddcols[ seq.int( from=4, to=length( ddcols), by=3)]
   dscols   <- ddcols[ seq.int( from=5, to=length( ddcols), by=3)]
   dmxcols  <- ddcols[ seq.int( from=6, to=length( ddcols), by=3)]
   dd[, row := 1:nrdd] # adds row number to show time sequence of executions
   dd[, run := rep( runname, nrdd)] # put run name in each row
   reshape( dd, list( timecols, dscols, dmxcols),
            v.names=c("Time", "D2", "Dmax"), timevar="group", idvar="row", 
            drop=c("time","d^2", "max d^2"), direction="long")
} # end read_diff
```

```{r}
#| label: ddb
#| warning: false
# warnings are generated because the columns of the diff files have no names.

diff_files <- list.files( td, glob2rx( "*h*.diff.txt"))
# the '*.h* will cause only the newly created heat/cool files to be read.
# call read_diff on each element of diff_files, and rbind into big data.table
ddb <- data.table::rbindlist( lapply( diff_files, 
                                      function(fn) read_diff( td, fn)))
head(ddb)
diffdata <- ddb[, .(d2mn = mean( D2), d2sd = sd( D2), maxD = max( Dmax)), 
                by=.( Time, run)]
# next line uses a regex to replace last 9 characters with nothing
diffdata[, run := gsub( '.{9}$', "", run)] # remove the ".diff.txt" part
head( diffdata, n=20)
nrow( diffdata)
```

As a reminder, each time from each run generates an entry in `ddb` and
this results in `r nrow(ddb)` rows.

### Fitting the Data

The next step is to fit each diffusion run's diffusion time series and
look for linear fits.

```{r}
#| label: fitdiff
fitdiff <- function( r, diffdata, plot=FALSE, weights = NULL, verbose = FALSE) { 
   # r is the run id as a string.
   # diffdata is a data.table with fields Time, run, d2mn (mean of the D2 data),
   #     Other fields are ignored.
   dd <- diffdata[ r == run,]
   # print( nrow(dd))
   maxT <- max( dd$Time)
   maxd <- max( dd$d2mn)
   if (!is.null(weights)) weights = 1 / dd$d2sd^2
   
   #lm0 <- lm( d2mn ~ Time - 1, data = dd)
   lm1 <- lm( d2mn ~ Time, data = dd, weights = weights)
   #lm2 <- lm( d2mn ~ poly( Time, 2), data = dd)
 
   if (plot) {
      newT <- data.frame( Time =c( 0, dd$Time)) # Predict value at Time = 0
      pred.w.plim <- predict( lm1, newT, interval = "prediction")
      pred.w.clim <- predict( lm1, newT, interval = "confidence")
      plot( d2mn ~ Time, data = dd, xlim = c( 0, maxT), ylim = c(0, maxd), 
              main = r, xlab = 'Time', ylab = expression( r^2))
      grid()
      if (!is.null( dd$d2sd)) 
         arrows( dd$Time, dd$d2mn - dd$d2sd, dd$Time, dd$d2mn + dd$d2sd,
                 length = 0.05, angle = 90, code = 3)
      matplot(newT, cbind( pred.w.clim, pred.w.plim[, -1]), 
              col = c( 1, 2, 2, 3, 3), lty = c(1,2,2,3,3), type = "l", 
              add = TRUE)
      #abline( lm1)
      abline( h = mean( dd$d2mn), lty = 4, col = 4)
      legend( x = 'bottomright',  pch = c(1, NA, NA, NA, NA), 
              lty = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 4), col = c( 1, 1, 2, 3, 4),
              legend = c("Measurements", 'Regression Line', "Conf. Interval",                            'Pred. Interval', 'Mean'))
   }
   if (verbose) {
      #print( summary( lm0))
      print( summary( lm1))
      #print( summary( lm2))
   }
   nr <- nrow( dd)
   mod <- summary( lm1)
   coeff <- unname( mod$coefficients[ "Time", c( 'Estimate', 'Std. Error')])
   t <- mod$fstatistic
   Fpvalue <-  stats::pf( t['value'], t['numdf'], t['dendf'], lower.tail=FALSE)
   data.table::data.table( run = r, nrd = nr, Estimated = coeff[1], 
      Std.Errord = coeff[2], r.squaredd = mod$r.squared, 
      Fvald =  unname( t['value']), Fpvalued = unname( Fpvalue), 
      dfd = t['dendf'])
} # end fitdiff
```

Here is an example of one run's data:

```{r}
fitdiff( "S3.0008h15", diffdata, plot = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)
```

### Updating `MD2DF.P` with Diffusion Data

The code below will update and save `MD2DF.P` using the `data.table`
*merge* idiom.

```{r}
#| label: MD2DF.P2
#| eval: false
#| # run this by hand to save a new file.
difflist <- unique( diffdata$run)
diffproc <- data.table::rbindlist( lapply( difflist, fitdiff, diffdata))
rm( difflist)
MD2DF.P[ diffproc, 
         `:=`( nrd = i.nrd, Estimated = i.Estimated, Std.Errord = i.Std.Errord, 
               r.squaredd = i.r.squaredd, Fvald = i.Fvald, 
               Fpvalued = i.Fpvalued, dfd = i.dfd), 
         on="run"]
saveRDS( MD2DF.P, file = "../MD2DF.P.RDS")
rm( diffproc)
```

```{r}
#| label: readMD2DF.P2
#| include: false
# this will execute when rendering, thus reading in the file saved above.
MD2DF.P <- readRDS( "../MD2DF.P.RDS")
```

# Analysis

## Diffusion

The diffusion itself holds no surprises, although the cooling cycle
retains its fluid state at a few lower temperatures (in runs that did
not exhibit valid equilibrium behavior). Since
$\left< r^2 \right> = 4 D t$, the minimum $D$ that will cause a particle
to move the mean inter-particle distance of
$a = \sqrt{2 \pi} / 3^{1/4} \approx 1.9046$ in time $t$ is
$D = a^2 / 4t$, or `r 2 * pi / sqrt(3) / (4 * 50)` at $t = 50\tau$.

```{r}
#| label: fig-D2vT
#| fig-cap: Difffusion estimate vs. temperature.  As before, red points are those not considerd valid. The blue vertical line is the start of diffusion for the `Init` points previously measured ($T = 0.01283$). The blue horizontal line is the threshold where the root-mean-square diffusion distance after $T = 50\tau$ (the maximum time over which diffusion was estimated) is equal to the mean particle distance $a = \sqrt{2 \pi / \sqrt{3}}$.
```

## Summary Statistics

We will plot the various statistics and draw some lines where melting
begins.

```{r}
#| label: S3DF
S3DF <- copy( MD2DF.P[ grepl( "S3", series),]) # subset all series 3 data
S3DF[ , rv := ke.sd.rs / ke.mean.rs] # add relative variance column
```

### Specific Heat via First Difference

We need to recreate the $dy/dx$ function.

```{r}
#| label: dydx

dydx <- function( y, x, lag = 1) {
   # find derivative over lag + 1 points
   lx <- length( x)
   stopifnot( length( y) == lx)
   data <- data.table( x = x, y = y, keyby = x)
   xm <- (data$x[ 1:(lx - lag)] + data$x[ (lag + 1):lx]) / 2 
   # midpoint of eval sets
   dydxfit <- function( i) { # get dy/dx from points i:(i + lag)
      c <- coef( lm( y ~ poly( x, lag, raw = TRUE), # get poly coef
                     data = data[ i:(i + lag)]))
      dpc <- (1:lag) * tail( c, -1) # derivative of poly coeff
      polyval( rev(dpc), xm[ i]) 
      # evaluate polynomial at midpoint of data & return
   }
   dd <- vapply( 1:(lx - lag), dydxfit, 1.0)
   list( dd=dd, xm = xm)
}

# test
tx <- c(1, 4, 3, 3.5, 2, 5)
ty <- tx^2
(dd <- dydx(ty, tx, 2)) # Note the NaN in third position: 3,  5, NaN, 7, 9
dd$dd - 2 * dd$xm
rm( tx, ty, dd) # remove these variables
```

Here we make a table we can use in a call to `xyplot()`

```{r}
#| label: fig-Cvbyhs
#| warning: false # log will produce som NaNs
#| fig-cap: First difference computation of the specific heat for each of the initialiation groups.
Cvbyhs <- by( S3DF[, .(ke.mean.rs, TE.mean.rs, hseries, itype)], S3DF$hseries, 
              with, c( hseries = unique(hseries), itype = unique( itype), 
                       dydx( TE.mean.rs, ke.mean.rs)))
# above returns a list of 9 elements: one for each hseries
# Note that the function called by 'by' is 'with', and the `dydx()` call is
#    passed as an extra parameter to `with`
# The following will create a table of Log(Cv) values
CvTable <- rbindlist( lapply( seq_along( Cvbyhs), function( i) {
   hs <- names( Cvbyhs[i]) # The series is now in the name is this sublist.
   x <- Cvbyhs[[i]]
   Cvlen <- length( x$dd)
   data.table( run = rep( NA, Cvlen), itype = rep( x$itype, Cvlen),
               hseries = rep( hs, Cvlen),
               valid = fifelse( x$xm %within% c( 0.01283, 0.014095),
                                FALSE, TRUE), 
               Temp = x$xm, variable = rep( "Log(Cv)", Cvlen),
               value = log( x$dd))
   }))
xyplot( value ~ Temp | hseries, data = CvTable[ Temp < 0.021], group = itype)
```

We will create a new table which will add in some data and set the order
of the data.
$C_v = 1 / \left( 1 - \frac{N \left< (\delta T)^2 \right>}{T^2} \right)$
(where $N$ is the number of particles, and
$\left< (\delta T)^2 \right> / T^2$ is the relative temperature
variance), we will threshold `Fpvalued` to a minimum of $10^{-15}$ and
takes its logarithm, and remove the factor of four from `Estimated` to
get $D$.

```{r}
#| label: S3DFd2ss 
S3DFd2ss <- S3DF[,.( run, itype, Temp = ke.mean.rs, hseries, 
                     valid = fifelse( valid == 1, TRUE, FALSE), 
                     # Values below are those plotted, hopefully in this order
                     TE = TE.mean.rs,
                     Pressure = Pressure.mean.rs,
                     rv,
                     D = Estimated / 4.0, 
                     LogFp = log( pmax( 1e-15, Fpvalued)), 
                     psiavg, psiabs = psiabs.mean.rs, 
                     Cv = 1 / (1 - 256 * rv^2))]
```

## Reorganizing Table

To plot all of the data, we need to make a long-form table. First, we
need to `melt()` the data table.

```{r}
#| label: S3DFd2m
# First select just the columns we're interested in

id.var = c( "run", "Temp", "valid", "itype", "hseries")
S3DFd2m <- melt( S3DFd2ss, id.var = id.var, direction = 'long', 
                 variable.name = 'variable', variable.factor = TRUE,
                 value.name = 'value') 
# now each variable is its own table.

S3DFd2m2 <- rbind( S3DFd2m, CvTable)
S3DFd2m2[, `:=`(variable = factor( variable, levels = unique( variable)),
                itype = factor( itype), hseries = factor(hseries))]
# giving the variable factor levels will cause xyplot to NOT sort it.
setkeyv( S3DFd2m2, c( "variable", "Temp"))
head( S3DFd2m2)
```

We now have each run with its temperature, the `valid` flag, the
`itype`, the `hseries`, the variable, and the *value* of each variable.

## Detecting Melting

We have a number of ways to detect phase changes, and nine series in
which to detect them.

1.  Start of diffusion (using `stepdet()`)
2.  Max relative temperature variance
3.  The `Fpvalued` being less than 1%.
4.  Detecting a point whose value is 5 or 7$\sigma$ beyond a lines fit
    in the Isochor (using `linedet()`)
    a.  Two going up in temperature
    b.  one going down in temperature.
5.  Max $C_v$
    a.  For first difference method, and
    b.  for $\left< (\delta T)^2 \right>$

The first step is to define the two functions mentioned above.

```{r}
#| label: stepdet
stepdet <- function( x, nsig = 3, nstart = 10, verbose = FALSE) {
  # x is a numeric vector
  # nsig is the number of standard deviations from the running mean x[i] must
  # \depart to be considered a step.
  # nstart is the number of points to start the running mean.
  # x <- x[ !is.na(x)] # drop any NA values before length test.
  stopifnot( length( x) > nstart +1)
   if (verbose) print( x)
  
  cumdet <- function( state, new){
    # state is a list with the following elements:
    #   sx: cumsum of x
    #   ss: the sum of squares
    #   n: the number of points in the running mean
    #   nv: the count when first detected
    # new is a new value to add to the running mean.
    if (state$nv == 0 ) { # only do this if we haven't detected a departure
      meanx <- state$sx / state$n 
      sdx <- sqrt( (state$ss - state$n * meanx^2)/ (state$n - 1)) 
      if (verbose) {
         #print(state)
         print( c( meanx, sdx))
      }
      if( abs( new - meanx) < (nsig * sdx)) { # nothing detected
        state$sx <- state$sx + new
        state$ss <- state$ss + new^2
        state$n <- state$n + 1
        state$nv <- 0
      } else { # departure detected
        state$nv <- state$n + 1
      }
    } # simply return state.
    return( state)
  }
  sxs <- sum( x[ 1:nstart])
  sss <- sum( x[ 1:nstart]^2) #sum squared start.
  s <- list( sx = sxs, ss = sss, n = nstart, nv = 0)
  if (verbose) print( s)
  Reduce( cumdet, x[(nstart + 1):length( x)], init = s)
}

(testcumdet <- stepdet( tx <- c( rnorm(20), 5 + rnorm(10)))) # n=20, nv=21
```

```{r}
#| label: linedet
linedet <- function( x, y, level = 0.99, nstart = 10) {
  # x & y are a numeric vectors of the same length
  # nsig is the probability that a noise deviation will cause a false detection
  #   over the total run of points.
  # depart to be considered a step.
  # nstart is the number of points to start the running mean.
  lx <- length( x)
  stopifnot( lx > nstart +1)
  stopifnot( lx == length( y))
  dt <- data.table( x = x, y = y)
  for ( i in nstart:(lx - 1)) { # step through looking for a departure
    pr <- predict( lm( y ~ x, data = dt[ 1:i,]), 
                   newdata = data.frame( x = x[ i + 1]), 
                   interval = "prediction", level = level)
    # cat( i, pr, "\n")
    if (!(y[ i + 1] %within% pr[, c("lwr","upr")])) { # if departure detected
      return( c( nv = i + 1, x = x[ i + 1], y = y[ i + 1],
                 pred = pr[1, 1], lwr = pr[1, 2], upr = pr[1, 3]))
      } # if (!(y...)
  } # for ( i...)
  # if we get here, there was no detection (if above was never TRUE)
  return( c( nv = NA, x = NA, y = NA,
                 pred = pr[1, 1], lwr = pr[1, 2], upr = pr[1, 3]))
}

tx <- 1:30
ty <- tx + rnorm(30)
ty[ 21:30] <- ty[ 21:30] + 5
(testcumdet <- linedet( x = tx, y = ty)) # nv=21, x=20
```

```{r}
#| include: false
rm( tx, ty, testcumdet) # remove test variables.
```

Next we'll make a function which we can hand a filtered long form
`data.table` and will return a record with the detection results.

```{r}
#| label: detect
detect <- function( data, nsig = 3, nstart = 10, level = 0.99) {
   # data is an MD2DF data.table SORTED BY TEMPERATURE (ke.mean.rs)
   # nsig is the number of standard deviations for stepdet to detect start 
   #     of diffusion
   # nstart is the number of points to include in the start of running means 
   #     or regression lines.
   # level is the significance threshold to exceed to call a line departure 
   #     a detection
   #  
   #  Returns a vector of temperatures at which detections occurred, and a 
   #  string vector describing each detection.
   setkey( data, Temp)
   subs <- subset( data, variable == "D" & !is.na( value))
   # not all records have diffusion estimates.
   sd <- stepdet( subs$value, nsig, nstart)
   detects   <- c( diff = subs$Temp[ sd$nv])
   detectsex <- c( diff = "Start of diffusion (stepdet)")
   subs <- subset( data, variable == "Cv")
   detects   <- c( detects,   maxCv = subs$Temp[ which.max( subs$value)])
   detectsex <- c( detectsex, maxCv = "Max Cv via rv")
   subs <- subset( data, variable == "Log(Cv)")
   detects   <- c( detects,   maxLCv = subs$Temp[ which.max( subs$value)])
   detectsex <- c( detectsex, maxLCv = "Max Cv via 1st diff")   
   subs <- subset( data, variable == "rv")
   detects   <- c( detects,   Maxrv = subs$Temp[ which.max( subs$value)])
   detectsex <- c( detectsex, Maxrv = "Max relative Temp variance")
   subs <- subset( data, variable == "LogFp" & value < log(0.01))
   detects   <- c( detects,   LogFp = subs$Temp[ 1])
   detectsex <- c( detectsex, LogFp = "Start of Diff (Fp < 0.01)")
   subs <- subset( data, variable == "Pressure")
   detects   <- c( detects,
                   Icld1 = subs$Temp[ linedet( x = subs$Temp, 
                                                y = subs$value, 
                                                nstart = nstart, 
                                                level = level)["nv"]])
   detectsex <- c( detectsex, Icld1 = "Isochor Solid1 (linedet)")
   detects   <- c( detects,
                   Icld2 = subs$Temp[ linedet( x = subs$Temp, 
                                                y = subs$value, 
                                                nstart = nstart, 
                                                level = 0.99999)["nv"]])
   detectsex <- c( detectsex, Icld2 = "Isochor Solid2 (linedet 5 nines)")
   setorder( subs, -Temp) # Reverse order
   detects   <- c( detects,
                   Icld3 = subs$Temp[ linedet( x = subs$Temp, 
                                                y = subs$value, 
                                                nstart = nstart, 
                                                level = 0.99)["nv"]])
   detectsex <- c( detectsex, Icld3 = "Isochor Fluid (linedet)")
   return( list( detects = detects, ex = detectsex))
}
```

The following created a `data.table` from each `hseries`:

```{r}

               function( x) {
```

@fig-Transition below shows plots of eight statistics. `Log(Cv)` is the
Log of the specific heat calculated by numerical differentiation across
heating/cooling series (i.e., `Init`, `0008`, etc.) as `lag = 1`;
(estimates where the temperature between 0.01283 and 0.014095
arbitrarily colored as not considered valid). `TE` is total energy, `rv`
is the relative temperature variance (the variance of the 500-point
re-sampled temperatures divided by the temperature mean), `psiavg` is
the magnitude of the average of $\psi$ (i.e., the step-by-step average
of the complex quantity) and `psiabs` is the step-by-step average of the
magnitude of $\psi$. `D` is the estimate of diffusion, `LogFp` is the
natural log of the probability of F-value of the diffusion regression of
$\left< R^2(t) \right> \sim t$ (where $t$ is time;). Low probabilities
indicate that that the regression line was unlikely caused by random
noise, and thus diffusion was present. The vertical red dashed lines
mark the detected transitions according to the `Init` heating/cooling
series.


Very little consistency there. Only the `Init` `hseries` really found
the first solid transition, and the temperature spacing between the
heating and cooling groups is so large that there is a large variance of
the transition temperatures. @fig-dtbyh below shows the delta achieved
at each temperature by `hseries`.

```{r}
#| label: fig-dtbyh
#| fig-cap: Change in temperature between adjacent samples (after sorting by temperature), plotted against mean temperature for each `hseries` group. The `Init` group had very small spacing in temperature.
dtbyh <- rbindlist( lapply( levels( S3DFd2m2$hseries), 
               function( x) {
                  y <- sort( 
                     S3DFd2m2[ hseries == x & variable == "TE" & Temp < 0.021,
                                 Temp])
                  data.table( dT = diff( y), 
                              Temp = (head( y, -1) + tail( y, -1)) / 2, 
                              hseries = x)
                  }))
xyplot( dT ~ Temp | hseries, data = dtbyh, group = hseries)
```

As the system goes into the transition region, added or subtracted
kinetic energy goes to or comes from potential energy, so the $\Delta T$
is small. Note that this doesn't occur with the `Init` group as it was
initialized to a particular kinetic energy and there there is no energy
change between runs. @fig-debyh below shows the same plot for the energy
change between runs.

```{r}
#| label: fig-debyh
#| fig-cap: The change in total energy between adjacent samples, plotted agains the mean total energy between samples, after sorting by total energy.
debyh <- rbindlist( lapply( levels( S3DFd2m2$hseries), 
               function( hs) {
                  y <- sort( 
                     S3DFd2m2[ hseries == hs & variable == "TE" & Temp < 0.021,
                                 value])
                  #cat( hs, y, "\n", sep = ": ")
                  data.table( dE = diff( y), 
                              TE = (head( y, -1) + tail( y, -1)) / 2, 
                              hseries = hs)
                  }))
xyplot( dE ~ TE | hseries, data = debyh, group = hseries)
```
